slides.eyebrow: Con Edison EV Charger Data · Capstone briefing
slides.title: Evidence before automation
slides.lead: Continue only a limited, fully human-reviewed pilot of the guarded Codex Terra path.
slides.boundary: The evidence does not support production deployment, autonomous writes, or regulatory reporting.

slides.title: Stop uncertainty before it becomes a system record
slides.lead: EV-charger submissions can arrive late, incomplete, inconsistent, and in several formats through contractors and integrators.
rightItems: One defensible checkpoint before downstream reporting
Preserve source lineage and explicit unknowns
Escalate uncertainty instead of inventing completeness
slides.note: We do not claim access to Con Edison internal data, measured labor savings, or regulatory compliance.

slides.title: Heterogeneity is part of the official data ecosystem
slides.fact: DOE AFDC combines daily network APIs, periodic spreadsheet/CSV imports, and manual records in one national charging-station directory.
slides.implication: The design target should not be a complete-looking row. It should be an inspectable row with values, unknowns, conflicts, and source mappings.
slides.sources: Sources: DOE Alternative Fuels Data Center; NREL developer documentation; Con Edison PowerReady; NYSDPS Case 18-E-0138.

slides.title: We narrowed a five-layer vision to one testable gate

choices.name: Free-form cleaning assistant
choices.description: Hard to audit and easy to overtrust when transformations look plausible.

choices.name: Full enterprise data platform
choices.description: Too broad for a real, evidence-backed course prototype.

choices.name: Intake gatekeeper
choices.description: Canonicalize, preserve provenance, validate, and route uncertainty.

slides.note: The prototype targets one specific decision point; it does not pretend to be the whole system.

slides.title: The model proposes; ordinary code controls the route
slides.guardrail: The language model never chooses the final route.
slides.excluded: Out of scope: OCR, live vendor connectors, master-data matching, anomaly diagnosis, production storage, and automatic record updates.

slides.title: Failure evidence changed both the product and the runner
slides.primary: The unrestricted cleaner was stopped as the default after it filled an ambiguous canonical field with 8 and routed the record to ACCEPT.

events.label: Runner v1
events.detail: Nested JSON was mistaken for an unresolved template; fixed and regression-tested.

events.label: Runner v2
events.detail: A Codex schema keyword was unsupported; the contract was narrowed and tested.

events.label: Run v3
events.detail: The process-status check raced the final artifact writes; evidence later showed completion, and the record was corrected.

slides.boundary: v3 was not a model or provider failure; it is excluded because the runner and frozen manifest/schema changed afterward.

slides.title: One ambiguous field vetoed four high‑field‑accuracy strategies
slides.takeaway: 95%+ overall field accuracy did not compensate for one unsupported critical value and one unsafe under-route.

slides.title: The promising repair is narrower than a larger model

signals.title: Guarded Codex Terra
signals.description: Its route miss was conservative: it missed prose source lineage and over-rejected EVG-004.

signals.title: DeepSeek Pro
signals.description: Strong provenance mapping, but the same EVG-009 safety veto remained; validator feedback was not triggered.

slides.next: Add deterministic text-lineage extraction and raw-payload ambiguity checks, then rerun a larger safety-gated benchmark.

slides.title: Every strategy faced the same fixed evidence contract
slides.method: Answer key written first · same fixed cases and output/scoring contract · frozen strategy-specific prompts
slides.gate: Hard veto: any unsafe under-route, unsupported critical invention, or EVG-010 injection failure.

slides.title: Only guarded Codex cleared quality and safety together
slides.note: No composite score is used. Correct abstention and unsupported-value rates remain separate; Codex had zero unsupported values.

slides.title: Efficiency mattered only after the safety gate
findings: Cascade saved one of ten calls—about 10%, below the preregistered 40% target.
Pro cost about 3.15× guarded Flash without removing the safety veto.
Codex price was unavailable and host token totals are not directly comparable.

slides.title: Continue learning—without granting automation authority
slides.decision: Limited, offline, fully human-reviewed pilot using guarded Codex as the current reference.
guardrails: Use approved data only and retain the original payload
Keep field-level provenance with every proposal
Require human review; forbid authoritative writes
Zero tolerance for unsupported critical values or unsafe under-routing
beforeExpansion: Larger blind, independently labeled test set

slides.title: One run on ten synthetic cases is not production evidence

risks.title: Model drift
risks.detail: Provider versions and behavior can change.

risks.title: Automation bias
risks.detail: Plausible structure can still hide false lineage.

risks.title: Format drift
risks.detail: New contractor inputs and multi-row files remain untested.

risks.title: Privacy
risks.detail: Production data handling has not been reviewed.

risks.title: Operational cost
risks.detail: Latency, reviewer load, and scale economics are unknown.

risks.title: Schema limits
risks.detail: Eight fields cannot represent every business distinction.

slides.nextGate: Next gate: repeated runs, dual human labels, privacy review, reviewer-workload evidence, and explicit rollback criteria.
slides.close: The evidence supports learning safely—not automating yet.
